_bell_lilly_: In Brennmoor, Casimir Lilly was a farmhand. In V-F6, he is a number and a rifle. He has told everyone he intends to be a farmhand again.

Casimir Lilly traded a cigarette for a pinch of salt. Supper improved. The argument about the exchange rate did not. The transfer made Casimir Lilly a sniper. He spent the first hour learning where everything belonged, including himself.
_cs__customs_: Roland Customs arrived on Day 9 as a replacement. The men in S-C14 had been fighting for 9 days already and looked at his clean boots like a rumour from another world.
Word came down the line: Blackwater Canal is ours. Roland Customs shook hands with a corporal he had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.

Roland Customs fired twice at the enemy post. The second shot found Tobias Adammyers, badly wounded. Nobody nearby said anything. The clerk counted the names twice. Roland Customs is number 973 of the first thousand to answer the call, and wears the ribbon of the First Thousand. The Hegemony flag went up over Grey Mill. Roland Customs did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again.
Roland Customs thought about a sweetheart who has stopped writing on sentry tonight, and the night felt a little shorter.
_oliverjarrett: The quartermaster asked Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret to sign for the blanket. He examined the blanket and asked whether the holes were included.

Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret kept watch so that Zeno Ghostoftheas could sleep. Then Zeno kept watch so that Saint could. Neither slept. Mail came up the line with a letter for Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret. Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret borrowed a book with three readers already waiting in line. For once, everyone was impatient about something harmless.

A dog crosses no man's land at Verdel Ridge every night, fed by Emil Majormalprac on one side and Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret on the other. The Concord call it Patrol. The Hegemony call it Spy. Mail came up the line with a letter for Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret. Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
A new recruit would not eat with the others. Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret left a place at the end of the bench and said nothing about it.
Blackwater Canal is in Hegemony hands. Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.

A bullet clipped Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret's helmet at S-S7 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Shot by Ivo "Crow" Natecartw of the Concord (@natecartw). Mail came up the line with a letter for Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret. Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret read it in the dugout and kept the envelope. The company read out the roll of the First Thousand at the dawn watch. Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret answered to number 418. Day 11. The Hegemony took Grey Mill. From the heights Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret could see the whole Concord line, and for the first time the war looked winnable.

Machine-gun fire swept S-S7. Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret took a round through the side and was carried back, grey in the face and very quiet. Shot by Florian Jacobsoifu of the Concord (@jacobsoifu). The bearers reached Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret at S-S7 too late. One shot, and it was over. Shot by Florian Jacobsoifu of the Concord (@jacobsoifu).
Casimir Oliverjarret put a frozen apple beside the bunk. Someone who had known Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret helped clear the shelf without saying why.
_sebs.c_: Nobody saw Konrad Sebs arrive. One morning there was simply one more helmet in R-F11, and a quiet rifleman under it.
Konrad Sebs was among the first hundred through the depot gates. The First Wave ribbon is the only clean thing he owns.
The transfer made Konrad Sebs a sniper. He spent the first hour learning where everything belonged, including himself.
Konrad Sebs hummed an old song from home on sentry. From the other side of the wire, very faintly, someone hummed it back.

Konrad Sebs saved half a biscuit for later. Later turned out to be six minutes away. After the loss of Verdel Ridge, Konrad Sebs helped stack spare sandbags at R-F11. Nobody asked when they would be needed.
A shell burst in the trench at R-F11. Konrad Sebs was thrown against the wall and did not get up. The bearers came at a run.

The bearers moved Konrad Sebs's stretcher against the wall at midday and back again at dusk. That was the whole schedule. A letter from home reached Konrad Sebs before dusk. Konrad Sebs read it twice and slept a little easier.

The medics would not give up on Konrad Sebs. On a stretcher in the open, between salvos, they kept him alive and then kept him whole. He returned to R-F11 today. A letter from home reached Konrad Sebs before dusk. Konrad Sebs read it twice and slept a little easier. The report confirmed the Hegemony victory at Hill 304. Konrad Sebs folded the paper so the headline stayed on the outside.
Konrad Sebs sang the first verse tonight, out loud. The other side sang the second. Nobody fired for an hour.

Konrad Sebs moved his hide three times today. Snipers who stay in one place do not stay anywhere for long. A letter from home reached Konrad Sebs before dusk. Konrad Sebs read it twice and slept a little easier.

An officer heard about the singing and forbade it. Tonight Konrad Sebs only whistled the first bar. Across the wire, someone whistled the last. A letter from home reached Konrad Sebs before dusk. Konrad Sebs read it twice and slept a little easier. The colonel pinned Konrad Sebs's posters to the dugout wall and read his words out at the dawn watch. From today he is the Propagandist of the Hegemony. He still keeps his rifle.

Somebody across the wire was singing. Then Nils Averelle stood up to sing louder, and Konrad Sebs fired. Nils Averelle was grazed. The singing stopped. Face blackened with soot, Konrad Sebs spent the night in a shell hole out in front of the wire. At first light Bram Satalik was grazed. A letter from home reached Konrad Sebs before dusk. Konrad Sebs read it twice and slept a little easier.

Konrad Sebs went over with the night raiders, found the enemy trench empty at that spot, and came back with a bag of their biscuits. Blackwater Canal has been won. Konrad Sebs listened as the corporal read the news twice, once for the men just off watch. A letter from home reached Konrad Sebs before dusk. Konrad Sebs read it twice and slept a little easier.

Konrad Sebs and Oskar "Whistle" Jozifanderso argued all night about whose hometown has the better beer. They agreed to finish the argument after the war. A letter from home reached Konrad Sebs before dusk. Konrad Sebs read it twice and slept a little easier. Grey Mill fell to the Hegemony at dusk. Konrad Sebs helped drag the guns up the slope and slept that night on ground nobody else had held for years.

Konrad Sebs did not want to shoot today. Then the enemy shot first, and Konrad Sebs fired back. Lucien Paulohwa was badly wounded. A bullet bounced off the trench wall and caught Konrad Sebs across the shin at R-F11. It bled a lot and meant very little. Shot by Tobias Guy of the Concord (@jurassic_guy013). A letter from home reached Konrad Sebs before dusk. Konrad Sebs read it twice and slept a little easier.
authentic.indonesian.patriot: Gustav Patriot walked into R-R10 on Day 9 and asked where the war was. A shell answered before anyone else could.
The Hegemony secured Blackwater Canal. Gustav Patriot helped pass the news along the line, checking each time that he had heard correctly.

The order came down the line: anything that moves. Something moved. Gustav Patriot fired, and Severin Masterofecli was grazed. Grey Mill has been won. Gustav Patriot listened as the corporal read the news twice, once for the men just off watch.
Gustav Patriot borrowed a magnifying glass to read cramped handwriting. The urgently needed word turned out to be 'cabbage'.
colt2real: Rafael Real told the sergeant he was a dance-hall violinist. The sergeant said the war needed one of those like it needed a hole in the roof, and put him on sentry.
From Blackwater Canal the Hegemony guns have a clear view. Rafael Real wrote to a girl from the dance hall, maybe that night and said only: 'We will take it back.'

Rafael Real fired twice at the enemy post. The second shot found Pavel Finnius, grazed. Nobody nearby said anything. A thousand names now stand in the regimental book. Rafael Real is number 848. The sergeant pinned the ribbon of the First Thousand on without a speech. Day 11: Grey Mill was lost. Rafael Real wrote down the news without trying to explain it.
In reserve, Rafael Real slept nine hours in a barn. He dreamt of nothing, which was the best part.
declan.117: Otto "Tin" Declan reached Q-F7 expecting a speech. The welcome consisted of a mug, a space on a bench and directions to the latrine.
Blackwater Canal fell to the Hegemony. Otto "Tin" Declan kept the newspaper; he wanted to remember exactly what had been promised beforehand.

Bastian Nerrdworx saw Otto "Tin" Declan freeze up on the fire step at the Sunken Road. Bastian said nothing, just stood closer. It was enough. News of the loss of Grey Mill reached Q-F7 with the rations. Otto "Tin" Declan ate while listening to the revised orders.

Machine-gun fire swept Q-F7. Otto "Tin" Declan took a round through the side and was carried back, grey in the face and very quiet. Shot by Quentin "Crow" Bannerlordsa of the Hegemony (@bannerlordsarp). Otto "Tin" Declan was killed at Q-F7 just after dawn. The cup of tea beside him was still hot. Shot by Quentin "Crow" Bannerlordsa of the Hegemony (@bannerlordsarp).
The papers say Cyril Declan. The sergeant says he has his older brother's eyes. Otto "Tin" Declan's eyes. Nobody in Q-F7 argues.
dinhdong234: They issued Konrad "Crow" Dinhdong a rifle, a spade and a number. He kept a pressed cornflower in his breast pocket, where the shrapnel would have to go through it first.
Konrad "Crow" Dinhdong raised his head for a heartbeat too long at S-F19. The bullet only grazed him. He will not do it again. Shot by Leopold "Brick" Moovin of the Concord (@da_moovin).

There were too few medics and too many wounded. Konrad "Crow" Dinhdong waited too long, and the wound grew worse for it. The Hegemony took Hill 304, and the orders at S-F19 changed before the cheering ended. Konrad "Crow" Dinhdong shouldered another load.
The medics would not give up on Konrad "Crow" Dinhdong. On a stretcher in the open, between salvos, they kept him alive and then kept him whole. He returned to S-F19 today.
A bullet went through Konrad "Crow" Dinhdong's sleeve at S-F19 and took some skin with it. He kept the sleeve. Shot by Florian Monkey of the Concord (@autistic_monkey3).
Konrad "Crow" Dinhdong walked back up the communication trench to S-F19, slower than before, but on his own feet.
Konrad "Crow" Dinhdong (Hegemony) and Dorian Maxhuntertat (Concord) spotted the same abandoned cart near Sorrow Copse. A long exchange of shots left the cart exactly where it was.

Konrad "Crow" Dinhdong was on the dawn watch at S-F19 when the Concord raiders came. A club, a shout, and Konrad "Crow" Dinhdong was on the trench floor waiting for the medic. Raider: Albin Warhamster of the Concord (@warhamster4). Blackwater Canal is in Hegemony hands. Konrad "Crow" Dinhdong watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.

Back on the fire step at S-F19. Konrad "Crow" Dinhdong says the wound itches, which the medics say is a good sign. A thousand names now stand in the regimental book. Konrad "Crow" Dinhdong is number 252. The sergeant pinned the ribbon of the First Thousand on without a speech. Konrad "Crow" Dinhdong walked the captured trenches of Grey Mill and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir.
The listening post reported scraping beyond the wire. Konrad "Crow" Dinhdong waited through an hour of it before a loose stake was found.
florian_dbd: Hugo Dbd walked into N-F10 on Day 11 and asked where the war was. A shell answered before anyone else could. The Hegemony won Grey Mill. In N-F10, Hugo Dbd listened to three explanations and trusted none of them.
A rat has started sitting on the ammunition box next to Hugo Dbd's bunk. He has named it Napoleon. A letter from home reached Hugo Dbd before dusk. Hugo Dbd read it twice and slept a little easier.
il_migliore_al_mondo: Gustav Mondo arrived on Day 9 as a replacement. The men in R-S16 had been fighting for 9 days already and looked at his clean boots like a rumour from another world.

Fresh from training, Gustav Mondo still aims the way the instructor said. Today it worked: Viktor "Rabbit" Daxmunro, grazed. Day 10. The Hegemony took Blackwater Canal. From the heights Gustav Mondo could see the whole Concord line, and for the first time the war looked winnable.

Gustav Mondo laughed at something nobody else had heard. Asked to share it, he admitted remembering a conversation from years ago. The clerk counted the names twice. Gustav Mondo is number 609 of the first thousand to answer the call, and wears the ribbon of the First Thousand. The Hegemony took Grey Mill, and the orders at R-S16 changed before the cheering ended. Gustav Mondo shouldered another load.
A replacement turned out to be from Greyhallow too. Gustav Mondo and the newcomer argued about the same bakery for half the night.
jacoorb: On Day 10 Florian Jacoorb took a post at Q-F4 that had been empty for two nights. He did not ask why. He polishes his buttons every evening, and the men liked him for it.

Florian Jacoorb was hit in the knee while crossing a low part of the trench at Q-F4. He will walk again, the medic thinks, but not soon. Shot by Roland Lesyk of the Concord (@eh_its_lesyk). Day 11. The Hegemony took Grey Mill. From the heights Florian Jacoorb could see the whole Concord line, and for the first time the war looked winnable.
Florian Jacoorb lay on a stretcher under a canvas sheet and watched the orderlies carry men in and out. Nobody had time to talk.
jesus.gr9: On Day 4 Wendel Jesus took a post at R-F4 that had been empty for two nights. He did not ask why. He counts everything: steps, shells, stars, and the men liked him for it.

Wendel Jesus and Florian Wubbarn made a pact on sentry tonight: whoever gets home first visits the other's family. They shook on it. A letter from home found Wendel Jesus before the night shift. Wendel Jesus folded it small and kept it close.

Wendel Jesus tried to write neatly for the first line of a letter. By the third, he was writing as quickly as the thoughts arrived. A letter from home found Wendel Jesus before the night shift. Wendel Jesus folded it small and kept it close. Hill 304 has been won. Wendel Jesus listened as the corporal read the news twice, once for the men just off watch.

Wendel Jesus had been watching the same gap for an hour. When Leopold "Saint" Joha crossed it, Wendel Jesus fired. Leopold "Saint" Joha was badly wounded. A letter from home found Wendel Jesus before the night shift. Wendel Jesus folded it small and kept it close.
Wendel Jesus taught Benedikt "Smokes" Lfer to play the harmonica. The whole squad has asked them both, politely, to stop.

Wendel Jesus saw Teodor Roos freeze up on the fire step at Sorrow Copse. Wendel said nothing, just stood closer. It was enough. A letter from home found Wendel Jesus before the night shift. Wendel Jesus folded it small and kept it close.

Wendel Jesus saw shapes coming through the gap in the wire and fired along it. The shapes went to ground. One of them was Casimir "Lucky" Localfilipin, grazed. A letter from home found Wendel Jesus before the night shift. Wendel Jesus folded it small and kept it close.

The flare went up just as Wendel Jesus reached the Concord parapet. Wendel Jesus jumped down first. Clement Geronimoleys was the man waiting there, and Clement Geronimoleys fell. (@geronimoleysen) Blackwater Canal fell to the Hegemony at dusk. Wendel Jesus helped drag the guns up the slope and slept that night on ground nobody else had held for years. A letter from home found Wendel Jesus before the night shift. Wendel Jesus folded it small and kept it close.

Wendel Jesus saw a helmet rise behind the enemy sandbags at R-F4 and fired once. Pavel Rozzyadog was grazed. A letter from home found Wendel Jesus before the night shift. Wendel Jesus folded it small and kept it close. The clerk counted the names twice. Wendel Jesus is number 253 of the first thousand to answer the call, and wears the ribbon of the First Thousand. The Hegemony secured Grey Mill. Wendel Jesus helped pass the news along the line, checking each time that he had heard correctly.

A grenade fragment found Wendel Jesus's shoulder. He calls it a souvenir and refuses to be sent back. A letter from home found Wendel Jesus before the night shift. Wendel Jesus folded it small and kept it close.
just_karter_k: The new machine gunner is Gustav Karter, once a brewer from Millbank. The corporal asked if a brewer was any use in a trench. Gustav Karter said he would find out.

Gustav Karter saw a hare run the whole length of no man's land and nobody on either side fired at it. Mail came up the line with a letter for Gustav Karter. Gustav Karter read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Gustav Karter spent the night in no man's land with pliers and a roll of wire. Every flare meant lying flat in the mud. The gap at R-F22 is closed now. Mail came up the line with a letter for Gustav Karter. Gustav Karter read it in the dugout and kept the envelope. The Hegemony flag went up over Hill 304. Gustav Karter did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again.

Gustav Karter sharpened a pencil carefully and then could not think what to write. He put the date at the top anyway. Mail came up the line with a letter for Gustav Karter. Gustav Karter read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Gustav Karter put an empty tin under a short table leg. Supper stopped sliding toward the corporal. Mail came up the line with a letter for Gustav Karter. Gustav Karter read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

The gun at R-F22 jammed twice and fired once. Once was enough: Oskar Davis, gravely wounded. Mail came up the line with a letter for Gustav Karter. Gustav Karter read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Gustav Karter taught Albin Sem three words in the language of home. Albin uses all three at the wrong moment, every day. Mail came up the line with a letter for Gustav Karter. Gustav Karter read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

On Day 10, Blackwater Canal passed to the Hegemony. Gustav Karter wrote the name in his diary with unusual care. Mail came up the line with a letter for Gustav Karter. Gustav Karter read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Gustav Karter reads Clement "Hollow" Lancegribko's letters from home out loud, because Hollow never learned to read. Gustav leaves out the sad parts. Hollow knows. Gustav Karter got a narrow grey ribbon today, the ribbon of the First Thousand. Number 307. The men who came later will ask about it. The Hegemony took Grey Mill, and the orders at R-F22 changed before the cheering ended. Gustav Karter shouldered another load.

Gustav Karter had marked the enemy's path to the latrine on a scrap of paper. Today it paid off: Silas Punchworth, badly wounded. Mail came up the line with a letter for Gustav Karter. Gustav Karter read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
liamroberts141: Isidor Liamroberts came up with a draft of replacements on Day 9. Nobody asked his name until the third night. After that, everyone knew it.

Isidor Liamroberts jumped into the Hegemony trench and swung the shovel at the first shape that moved. It was Edmund Ahmadhcj. The Hegemony medics will be busy. (@ahmadhcj07) Isidor Liamroberts went over with the raiders and dropped into the Hegemony trench. Casimir Sky was hit hard before the whistle called everyone back. (@the_ghost_of_sky) The Hegemony raiders came over at R-C8 in the middle of the night. Isidor Liamroberts met them first and did not survive the fight. Killed in the night raid by Dorian Yoollyfox of the Hegemony (@yoollyfox).
Yann Liamroberts came to the front because his cousin Isidor Liamroberts never came home. He carries his mother's thimble.

Yann Liamroberts got a photo of the family house. He spent longer looking at the strange curtains than at the faces. Yann Liamroberts got a narrow grey ribbon today, the ribbon of the First Thousand. Number 635. The men who came later will ask about it. Grey Mill fell to the Hegemony. Yann Liamroberts kept the newspaper; he wanted to remember exactly what had been promised beforehand.
Yann Liamroberts was made Lance Corporal. He celebrated by sleeping four hours in a row.
ma.rley5115: Day 3: Yann "Parson" Rley reached R-F7 with a full packet of cigarettes. Learning everyone's name proved remarkably easy. The report confirmed that the Concord held Verdel Ridge. Yann "Parson" Rley read the last line twice, looking for something the first reading had missed.
Yann "Parson" Rley tried to remember the sound of the church bell in Varenne. Every version sounded like the ration bell.
A shell splinter the size of a fist hit Yann "Parson" Rley at R-F7. He is alive and he is in pain, and he needs a bed.

No bed for Yann "Parson" Rley yet. A medic checked the bandage and promised him a place as soon as one opened up. The Hegemony secured Hill 304. Yann "Parson" Rley helped pass the news along the line, checking each time that he had heard correctly.
Every bed was taken and every medic was busy. Yann "Parson" Rley died waiting. The men at R-F7 have not stopped talking about it.
The papers say Teodor "Doc" Rley. The sergeant says he has his uncle's eyes. Yann "Parson" Rley's eyes. Nobody in R-F7 argues.
Teodor "Doc" Rley counted the stitches in a darned sock while waiting for orders. Whoever fixed it had used three colors of wool.
Teodor "Doc" Rley brought back a wounded man and a lost machine gun from Sorrow Copse in one trip. He is Lance Corporal now.
Rumour reached R-F7 that the war would be over by spring. Teodor "Doc" Rley has heard it before. So has everyone.
On Day 10, Blackwater Canal passed to the Hegemony. Teodor "Doc" Rley wrote the name in his diary with unusual care.

A bullet clipped Teodor "Doc" Rley's helmet at R-F7 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Shot by Lucien Kattawar of the Concord (@max.kattawar). A thousand names now stand in the regimental book. Teodor "Doc" Rley is number 168. The sergeant pinned the ribbon of the First Thousand on without a speech. Day 11. The Hegemony took Grey Mill. From the heights Teodor "Doc" Rley could see the whole Concord line, and for the first time the war looked winnable.
The wound on Teodor "Doc" Rley's hand healed crooked, but it healed. He can hold a rifle and a mug, and those are the two things that matter.
madein_.cuba: "You're late," said the corporal when Bastian "Rabbit" Cuba arrived on Day 9. "Everyone's late. Get a spade."

Blackwater Canal has been won. Bastian "Rabbit" Cuba listened as the corporal read the news twice, once for the men just off watch. Bastian "Rabbit" Cuba became a runner today. He wrote the change in a letter home, then crossed out the explanation and tried again.

A newspaper reached Bastian "Rabbit" Cuba with the corner torn off. According to the half a sentence that survived, the war was going well. A letter from home found Bastian "Rabbit" Cuba before the night shift. Bastian "Rabbit" Cuba folded it small and kept it close. A thousand names now stand in the regimental book. Bastian "Rabbit" Cuba is number 844. The sergeant pinned the ribbon of the First Thousand on without a speech. Grey Mill fell to the Hegemony at dusk. Bastian "Rabbit" Cuba helped drag the guns up the slope and slept that night on ground nobody else had held for years.
Bastian "Rabbit" Cuba drew the street leading to Millbank. There was no room left for the last house, so he turned the page over.
melioduff_: The new chaplain is Wendel Melioduff, once a shepherd from Varenne. The corporal asked if a shepherd was any use in a trench. Wendel Melioduff said he would find out.
A man asked Wendel Melioduff to sit nearby without saying anything. He stayed until the man fell asleep.
Wendel Melioduff held a service beside a ration store. The men sang quietly so the sleepers behind the wall could rest.
Wendel Melioduff reads Arno Passenger's letters from home out loud, because Arno never learned to read. Wendel leaves out the sad parts. Arno knows.
The relief column arrived early. Wendel Melioduff made room in the shelter by moving everything except the men already asleep.
Victory at Blackwater Canal. Wendel Melioduff let himself talk about leave for the first time in days.

Wendel Melioduff opened a parcel addressed in unfamiliar handwriting. A note inside said the usual writer had hurt a wrist. He read that note first. The company read out the roll of the First Thousand at the dawn watch. Wendel Melioduff answered to number 430. Grey Mill is in Hegemony hands. Wendel Melioduff watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.
Wendel Melioduff has learned to recognize the ration cart by its squeaky wheel. This afternoon, a different squeak caused real disappointment.
no_one_here_to_check: Karel Check was a baker in Saint-Lune until the posters went up. He came to R-F10 with his mother's thimble, and within a day the whole bay knew that he counts everything: steps, shells, stars.
Karel Check, volunteer number 67, received the First Wave ribbon. The quartermaster pronounced the name wrong; he corrected it for the record.
Karel Check opened a parcel addressed in an unfamiliar hand. Inside was a note explaining that the usual letter writer had hurt a wrist. He read that note first.
News of the loss of Verdel Ridge reached R-F10 with the rations. Karel Check ate while listening to the revised orders.
Karel Check and Isidor "Rabbit" Hayden sat through a quiet hour without finding anything to say. At the change of watch, the next pair was told it had been a good hour.
Karel Check was promoted to Lance Corporal. The first request addressed to the new rank concerned a blocked drain.

A football came over the parapet from the Concord side with Quentin "Mud" Sperring's name scratched on it. Karel Check kicked it back. It did not come again. The Hegemony took Hill 304, and the orders at R-F10 changed before the cheering ended. Karel Check shouldered another load.
Dawn watch. Karel Check put a round across no man's land and the enemy line went quiet: Anselm "Parson" Rock, badly wounded.
Karel Check followed a cough through the fog and found the ration party stuck at a junction. For once, a cough improved supper.
Fog so thick that Karel Check could not see the end of his own rifle. Somewhere out there, someone was whistling.
Someone had used a newspaper to wrap the onions. Karel Check read a theatre review while peeling supper.

At R-F10 a shape dropped into the trench out of the night. Karel Check turned around and took a shovel blow. Nils Ewalters of the Concord was already gone. Raider: Nils Ewalters of the Concord (@ewalters120). Karel Check walked the captured trenches of Blackwater Canal and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir.

Machine-gun fire swept R-F10. Karel Check took a round through the side and was carried back, grey in the face and very quiet. Shot by Gustav "Mud" Stefano of the Concord (@faccio.stefano). Karel Check looked over the parapet at R-F10 for one second too long. The bullet came before the sound. Shot by Gustav "Mud" Stefano of the Concord (@faccio.stefano).

Edmund Check put his mother's thimble beside the bunk. Someone who had known Karel Check helped clear the shelf without saying why. Volunteer number 67. The quartermaster pinned the First Wave ribbon on Edmund Check's tunic and said: 'Don't let the mud have it.' The Hegemony flag went up over Grey Mill. Edmund Check did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again.
A round went through the rim of Edmund Check's helmet and nicked his ear on the way out. He has a notch in both now. Shot by Jonas Freddie of the Concord (@freddie55133).
omcc1740: Arno Omcc introduced himself as a ferryman from Rosenau. The corporal repeated the name correctly. That helped more than the advice.
Arno Omcc walked the captured trenches of Blackwater Canal and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir.

Arno Omcc lost at cards to the corporal and now owes him a week of tobacco and one favour, unspecified. Grey Mill is in Hegemony hands. Arno Omcc watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.
Gideon Hayden fell asleep on watch. Arno Omcc took over without waking Gideon, and told the sergeant nothing.
therealgu1ll0tine: Casimir "Ghost" Tine unpacked a pocket Bible with a hole in it at N-F13. The man in the next bunk shifted his bag to make room without asking what it was. From Grey Mill the Hegemony guns have a clear view. Casimir "Ghost" Tine wrote to a sweetheart who has stopped writing that night and said only: 'We will take it back.'
Casimir "Ghost" Tine cleaned the gun for the fourth time today. The gun is the only thing in the trench that is kept dry.
tom_w372: On Day 9, Karel Tom arrived during an argument about a missing spoon. The war already had matters more urgent than introductions.

The sergeant read out the order: Blackwater Canal has fallen, hold the line. Karel Tom looked at the new recruits coming up the road and counted them. The transfer made Karel Tom a sniper. He spent the first hour learning where everything belonged, including himself.

Karel Tom wrote the range on the back of a ration card: 380 yards. Then Karel Tom used it. Severin Xboxme was badly wounded. A letter from home found Karel Tom before the night shift. Karel Tom folded it small and kept it close. The Hegemony won Grey Mill. In Q-S11, Karel Tom listened to three explanations and trusted none of them.

Karel Tom took stock of his pockets: string, crumbs, a pencil and no sign of the button he was looking for. A letter from home found Karel Tom before the night shift. Karel Tom folded it small and kept it close.
xavidonegan: They issued Emil "Brick" Xavidonegan a rifle, a spade and a number. He kept a lucky button in his breast pocket, where the shrapnel would have to go through it first.
